attempted_claim: Let c,d in Q^x, E^c: y^2=x^3+c over Q with CM by Z[zeta_3], and Y=Kum(E^c x E^d) over Q with (Br(Y)/Br_1(Y))_{3^infty} nonzero and Br_1(Y)=Br(Q). Using the Skorobogatov-Zarhin description B([P,Q])=chi_P cup phi_*(chi_Q) and p-adic Hodge / formal-group analysis of E^c(Q_3), E^d(Q_3) and crystalline Frobenius on H^2_et(Y_{bar Q},Z_3(1)) at the ramified prime 3, compute the evaluation maps ev_{A,v}:Y(Q_v)->Br(Q_v)_{3^infty} for A generating the 3-primary transcendental part, and decide the dichotomy: does Y(A_Q)^{Br(Y)} nonempty imply Y(Q) Zariski dense in Y, with A obstructing weak approximation (non-constant at 3, constant at v!=3) but not density, or does A force Y(Q) into a proper closed subset?
decisive_failure: Lane resources were Python/sympy only with no crystalline or formal-group pairing machinery; the ramified-3 CM invariant classification and local evaluation at the always-bad prime 3 could not be completed; the key references explicitly defer the 3-primary Q(zeta_3) analysis; and the only completed density instance reproduces a published theorem rather than an original result.
